questions.title: What do SS-GEMM and RS-GEMM mean in FlashAttention-3, and how do they map to WGMMA sources?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 of the FlashAttention-3 paper (the forward pass without intra-consumer overlap), the authors label two GEMMs as "SS-GEMM" for computing $\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)} = \mathbf{Q}_i \mathbf{K}_j^\top$ and "RS-GEMM" for updating $\mathbf{O}_i$. I assume "S" means the operand is sourced from shared memory and "R" means from registers, but I'm not entirely sure which operand is where in each call. Can someone clarify the exact meanings of SS-GEMM vs. RS-GEMM in the context of Hopper's WGMMA (e.g., which operand is in SMEM vs RMEM in each case), and how these map to the asynchronous WGMMA calls used by the paper?

questions.title: How does the local softmax with running $m_i$ and $\ell_i$ yield the exact global softmax result?
questions.question_body: The paper uses the standard FlashAttention trick of maintaining a running max $m_i$ and a running normalizer $\ell_i$ per row while streaming over blocks of keys. At each step it computes $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)} = \exp(\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)} - m_i)$, updates $\ell_i = e^{m_i^{\mathrm{old}} - m_i}\,\ell_i + \mathrm{rowsum}(\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)})$, and rescales the partial $\mathbf{O}_i$. Could someone provide a short derivation showing that after processing all key/value blocks, the final $\mathbf{O}_i$ equals $\mathrm{softmax}(\alpha\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top)\mathbf{V}$ exactly (i.e., that the running rescalings do not introduce approximation), and explain why keeping softmax intermediates in FP32 preserves numerical stability?

questions.title: How does bar.sync enforce the pingpong overlap of softmax and GEMM across warpgroups without race conditions?
questions.question_body: The paper describes a "pingpong" schedule where two consumer warpgroups alternate: while one warpgroup is doing its softmax (MFU ops), the other is executing GEMMs (WGMMA), and vice versa. They mention using bar.sync to force GEMMs of warpgroup 1 to be scheduled before those of warpgroup 2 so the softmax overlaps with GEMMs. How exactly are the barriers placed to avoid deadlocks and races? What is the ordering constraint that guarantees: (1) GEMM0/GEMM1 of warpgroup 1 start before softmax of warpgroup 1, and (2) the softmax of warpgroup 1 runs while warpgroup 2 is in WGMMA, then they swap cleanly?

questions.title: What exactly are "commit" and "wait" for WGMMA/TMA on Hopper in this paper?
questions.question_body: Throughout the algorithms, the authors write instructions like "Commit and wait" or "Commit but do not wait" for WGMMA, and they describe TMA loads as asynchronous with a later wait. Which exact CUDA/PTX primitives are they referring to? For example: for TMA is this tma.load followed by barrier.arrive/wait or cp.async-style wait groups? For WGMMA, is this wgmma.mma_async with proxy/barrier semantics? A mapping from the pseudocode's commit/wait to concrete Hopper instructions or programming abstractions (e.g., CUTLASS APIs) would really help.

questions.title: How should I choose the number of stages $s$ in the circular SMEM buffer, and what are the trade-offs?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 uses an $s$-stage circular buffer in shared memory to pipeline TMA loads of $\{\mathbf{K}_j, \mathbf{V}_j\}$. How should $s$ be chosen on H100 in practice? What are the trade-offs in terms of: (1) SMEM footprint vs. occupancy, (2) latency hiding for TMA, and (3) added synchronization overhead? Is there a rule of thumb relating $s$ to the time of one WGMMA tile vs the TMA tile load time, or to the number of consumer warpgroups?

questions.title: In Algorithm 2, which operations are actually overlapped—does exp run while Tensor Cores execute WGMMA?
questions.question_body: In the 2-stage pipeline (Algorithm 2), the authors say the second WGMMA of iteration $j$ overlaps with softmax from iteration $j+1$. In concrete terms, which specific instructions overlap on Hopper: do the MFU exponentials and FP32 FMAs for softmax and rescaling execute concurrently with the Tensor Cores running wgmma.mma_async? A brief timeline for iterations $j$ and $j+1$ showing when waits happen for $\mathbf{Q}_i\mathbf{K}_j^\top$ vs. $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_{\text{cur}}\mathbf{V}_{j-1}$ and when softmax starts would help me reconcile the pseudocode with hardware reality.

questions.title: Can someone reproduce the 50% cycle estimate for exp vs matmul on H100 for head dimension 128?
questions.question_body: The paper estimates that for FP16, head dimension $d=128$, the exponential can take roughly 50% of the cycles: there are about $512\times$ more matmul FLOPs than exp ops in the forward pass, but exp has about $256\times$ lower throughput on H100, so exp ends up taking about half the time. Could someone show this computation step by step, including: (1) counting exp ops per token per block for softmax, (2) counting matmul FLOPs for $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$ and $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$, and (3) plugging in the quoted H100 FP16 Tensor Core throughput vs MFU exp throughput to arrive at the 50% figure?

questions.title: Where is causal masking applied in the pipelined loop, and does it interfere with overlap?
questions.question_body: For causal attention, where exactly is the mask applied in the overlapped 2-stage main loop? Is the mask applied as $-\infty$ to entries of $\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)}$ prior to computing $m_i$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)}$? Does this introduce additional data-dependent divergence or extra waits that could break the intended overlap between WGMMA and softmax, especially for tiles that straddle the triangular boundary?

questions.title: How does the in-kernel FP8 $\mathbf{V}$-tile transpose via LDSM/STSM work if transpose ops cannot split packed 8-bit pairs?
questions.question_body: For FP8 WGMMA, the paper says only k-major operands are supported, so $\mathbf{V}$ tiles must be transposed in-kernel. The authors use LDSM/STSM, packing two 8-bit values into one 16-bit lane, but mention that the transpose variants cannot split packed 8-bit entries, necessitating register moves between LDSM and STSM. Could someone describe a concrete sequence for one $8\times8$ microtile showing: (1) how bytes are packed for LDSM, (2) what register-level shuffles or byte permutes are applied, and (3) how STSM writes the transposed k-major layout back to SMEM—all without excessive register pressure?

questions.title: Accumulator/operand layout mismatch for FP8 WGMMA: how do the byte-permute reorderings preserve correctness?
questions.question_body: The paper notes that FP8 WGMMA's FP32 accumulator register layout differs from the FP8 operand-A layout, so they byte-permute the accumulator (e.g., reordering bytes from d0 d1 d4 d5 d2 d3 d6 d7, then repeating every 8 bytes) to make it a valid operand to the next FP8 WGMMA. They then also permute rows of the $\mathbf{V}$ tile to compensate. Could someone explain: (1) why Hopper exposes these two different register layouts, (2) how the specific byte-permute maps columns of the logical $\mathbf{P}$ tile, and (3) how matching the $\mathbf{V}$ row permutation recovers the original matrix product $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$ exactly?

questions.title: Block quantization math: how are per-block FP8 scales folded into the attention computation without extra FLOPs?
questions.question_body: The FP8 path uses per-block scales for $\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}$ (block quantization). Suppose $\mathbf{Q}_b = s_Q^{(b)}\,\hat{\mathbf{Q}}_b$ and $\mathbf{K}_c = s_K^{(c)}\,\hat{\mathbf{K}}_c$ for blocks $b,c$, with hats denoting FP8-quantized integers. Then a score block is $\mathbf{S}_{bc} = \alpha\, s_Q^{(b)} s_K^{(c)}\, \hat{\mathbf{Q}}_b \hat{\mathbf{K}}_c^\top$. How are these scales incorporated into: (1) the stable-softmax running $m_i,\ell_i$ updates, and (2) the $\mathbf{O}$ accumulation with $\mathbf{V}$ (which itself has per-block scale $s_V^{(c)}$), without adding extra GEMMs or elementwise passes? A small worked example over two K/V blocks would be great.

questions.title: Incoherent processing: is the random orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{M}$ fixed per head/layer or per block, and how is it stored/applied efficiently?
questions.question_body: To reduce outlier-induced quantization error, the paper multiplies $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{K}$ by a random orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{M}$ (Hadamard times random signs), exploiting $(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{M})(\mathbf{K}\mathbf{M})^\top = \mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$. Practical questions: (1) Is $\mathbf{M}$ fixed per layer and head, or randomized per sequence/minibatch, or even per block? (2) How is $\mathbf{M}$ stored (full matrix vs. implicit Hadamard/sign seeds)? (3) Is $\mathbf{M}$ fused with rotary embedding in practice, and does this fusion complicate training/backprop (e.g., gradients through $\mathbf{M}$ are trivial, but does it affect caching or recomputation)?

questions.title: How do you pick $B_r$ and $B_c$ given the extra registers for $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{next}}$ in the 2-stage pipeline?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 2 needs to keep an additional $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{next}}$ tile in registers to overlap softmax with GEMM, which increases register pressure by roughly $B_r \times B_c \times \mathrm{sizeof}(\text{float})$ per CTA (plus per-thread fragmentation). On Hopper, what heuristics do you use to pick $B_r$ (query rows per tile) and $B_c$ (key/value rows per tile) so that: (1) no spilling occurs, (2) occupancy is not crippled by setmaxnreg allocations to consumer warps, and (3) Tensor Cores remain fed? Any guidance for head dimensions $d\in\{64,128,256\}$?

questions.title: What exactly is "k-major" for FP8 WGMMA on Hopper, and how do the attention GEMMs map to that constraint?
questions.question_body: The paper states that FP8 WGMMA only supports k-major operands in SMEM. For a GEMM computing $A (M\times K) \times B^\top (N\times K)$, could someone define precisely what "k-major" means in terms of strides and layout? In the attention forward pass: (1) for $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$ which operand(s) must be k-major, and (2) for $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$, which operand must be k-major? How does this requirement lead to the need to transpose $\mathbf{V}$ tiles in-kernel if inputs are originally contiguous in the head dimension?

questions.title: What exactly is the FP8 baseline for the 2.6× RMSE improvement claim, and are comparisons apples-to-apples?
questions.question_body: In the numerical error section, the FP8 baseline is described as "per-tensor scaling, with matmul accumulator in FP32 and softmax intermediates in FP16." Meanwhile, FA-3 uses FP8 with block quantization and incoherent processing, and keeps key intermediates in FP32. To fairly interpret the 2.6× RMSE reduction: (1) are both methods using the same FP8 format (e4m3)? (2) Are the same operator precisions used for softmax, rescaling, and epilogue? (3) Is the only change per-tensor vs. per-block scaling and incoherent processing? If there are other differences (e.g., different accumulation or cast policies), can you enumerate them?

questions.title: Why is forward attention FLOPs computed as $4N^2 d H$, and why divide by 2 with causal masking?
questions.question_body: In the benchmarking section, the forward FLOPs are given as $4\cdot \text{seqlen}^2\cdot\text{head dimension}\cdot\text{number of heads}$. Could someone derive this? My attempt: each of the two GEMMs ($\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$ and $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$) costs about $2N^2 d$ per head, summing to $4N^2 d$ per head, then multiply by $H$. With causal masking, about half of the score matrix is not computed, hence divide by 2. Is this precisely correct when using block tiling and triangular masking, or is there a small deviation from exactly half because of tile edges?

questions.title: What is a "persistent kernel" in this context, and why does not having one for FP8 hurt short sequences?
questions.question_body: The discussion notes that FA-3 FP16 uses a persistent kernel and load balancing strategy, while FP8 FA-3 does not, which partly explains worse performance at short seqlens vs cuDNN FP8. Could someone explain what persistent kernels mean here (e.g., CTAs persist and pull multiple tiles/batches to amortize launch/latency), how load balancing is implemented across CTAs/warpgroups, and why the lack of persistence especially penalizes small workloads (e.g., launch overheads, underutilized SMs, poor overlap)?

questions.title: How is the in-kernel $\mathbf{V}$-tile transpose overlapped with GEMMs—who issues it and how are dependencies enforced?
questions.question_body: For the FP8 path the paper prefers transposing $\mathbf{V}$ tiles in-kernel using LDSM/STSM, and mentions that after the first iteration the next $\mathbf{V}$-tile transpose can be issued "in the shadow of" the GEMMs on the prior $\mathbf{V}$ and current $\mathbf{K}$. Concretely: (1) is the transpose executed by the producer warpgroup or by the consumer? (2) Which synchronization primitives ensure that the consumer never reads an untransposed $\mathbf{V}$ tile (e.g., separate barriers per stage for $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$)? (3) How is the circular buffer indexed so that transpose latency is hidden but buffer stages are safely reused?
